# blitcp

> blitcp is an open-source (Apache-2.0) high-speed file-transfer CLI for
> Linux, macOS and Windows. It reads files in physical disk order (FIEMAP /
> fcntl / FSCTL), deduplicates content with xxHash-128 hard links, streams
> over plain SSH with a tar pipe (no SFTP, nothing installed on the server),
> copies to S3 / Azure Blob / Google Cloud Storage, preserves sparse files
> via SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE, and hash-verifies every file after copying.

Key facts:

- Free and open source, Apache-2.0. Single Python CLI (`blitcp.py`) plus an
  optional desktop GUI; prebuilt binaries on GitHub Releases.
- Positioned as a faster alternative to cp, rsync, scp/SFTP, robocopy,
  FastCopy (the Windows tool, unrelated) and TeraCopy — with reproducible,
  cold-cache benchmarks published for every claim.
- Remote transfers run over a normal SSH connection using the remote's
  existing `tar` — works on Synology DSM and BusyBox NAS boxes, and on
  servers with SFTP disabled. Typically 3–5× faster than scp/SFTP on trees
  of small files.
- Deduplication: files are hashed (xxHash-128, SHA-256 fallback); duplicate
  content is copied once and hard-linked. Cross-run dedup via a persistent
  SQLite cache; `--index-existing` reflink-dedups against files already at
  the destination.
- Sparse files (VM disk images, Longhorn replicas): only allocated extents
  are read and holes are recreated, so a 2.3 TB logical set occupying
  12.2 GB copies as 12.2 GB.
- Cloud: s3:// (AWS, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2), az://,
  gs:// as source or destination, with named connections and AES-256-GCM
  encrypted credentials.
- Security: `--use-sudo` self-elevation with safety checks and an
  append-only `chattr +i` audit log; SSH host-key TOFU verification;
  hash-pinned self-updates.

## Docs

- [CLI reference](https://blitcp.dev/docs/): every flag, subcommand and
  endpoint form.
- [Local copies guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/local-copies/):
  folders, single files, globs, multi-source, USB/Windows.
- [SSH transfers guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/ssh-transfers/):
  tar-pipe push/pull/relay without SFTP.
- [Cloud storage guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/cloud-storage/):
  S3 / Azure / GCS endpoints and the creds manager.
- [Sparse files & VM images guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/sparse-files/):
  SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE extent walking, Longhorn and libvirt.
- [Sudo backups guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/sudo-backups/):
  root-level snapshots with a tamper-evident audit log.
- [Everyday options guide](https://blitcp.dev/docs/guide/everyday-options/):
  dry runs, excludes, buffer tuning, dedup toggles.

## Comparisons

- [blitcp vs rsync](https://blitcp.dev/compare/rsync/): cold-cache
  benchmark (8.19s vs 14.14s on 12,347 small files) and when rsync is still
  the better tool (incremental delta syncs).
- [blitcp vs Robocopy](https://blitcp.dev/compare/robocopy/): Windows
  benchmark (2m28s verify-on vs 3m16s) and robocopy's zero-install advantage.
- [blitcp vs TeraCopy](https://blitcp.dev/compare/teracopy/): 11.4 GB
  mixed workload (19m06s verify-on vs 25m20s verify-off).
- [blitcp vs cp](https://blitcp.dev/compare/cp/): 2.5× faster on
  rotational disks via physical-offset read ordering.
- [blitcp vs scp/SFTP](https://blitcp.dev/compare/scp/): one tar stream
  instead of per-file round-trips; ~3× faster on a 91,663-file push.
- [blitcp vs FastCopy](https://blitcp.dev/compare/fastcopy/): unrelated
  tools with similar names; 2m28s verify-on vs 3m38s verify-off on the same
  Windows workload.
- [All comparisons](https://blitcp.dev/compare/)

## Benchmarks

- [Benchmarks](https://blitcp.dev/benchmarks/): cold-cache, durable-write
  comparisons against cp, rsync, robocopy, FastCopy and TeraCopy, with every
  command listed for reproduction.

## Install

- [Windows install & verification](https://blitcp.dev/install/windows/):
  why SmartScreen appears (unsigned open-source binary) and how to verify
  downloads against GitHub's official SHA-256 digests.
